items.prompt: An array of length n receives 200,000 operations of the form “add delta to every index in inclusive [l, r]”. Only the final array is needed after all operations. Which representation is the decisive prefix-family choice?
constraints: No intermediate query must be answered.

options.text: Record a +delta change at l and a -delta change after r, then prefix-accumulate all changes once.
Immediately visit every index in [l, r] for each update.
Sort the array values before applying the updates.
Maintain one current window sum and move it between update ranges.

feedback.reason: The final effect changes only when an update becomes active at l and stops after r, so endpoints are sufficient until one reconstruction pass.

blocks.text: A difference array stores changes between adjacent final values rather than materializing every update immediately. Marking diff[l] += delta and diff[r + 1] -= delta causes the running prefix of diff to equal the active accumulated update at each index. This trades O(length of range) per update for O(1) marks and one O(n) pass.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.apply_every_element: Direct application is correct but can cost O(n) per update, producing O(un) work in the worst case. It ignores the endpoint cancellation structure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_update_ranges: The updates are positional. Sorting values changes which indices each range refers to and does not reduce the range-write cost.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.moving_window_sum: A window represents one active interval while scanning; it does not encode many overlapping future additions to reconstruct later.

items.prompt: After all endpoint marks are written, what does the running prefix of diff represent at index i?
constraints: Each update [l, r] adds +delta at l and -delta immediately after r when that boundary exists.

options.text: The original A[i] even before it is added to the accumulated delta.
The total delta from all updates whose ranges include index i.
The number of indices in one current moving window.
The number of update deltas smaller than A[i].

feedback.reason: Prefixing the boundary changes turns start and stop events into the cumulative update active at each position.

blocks.text: Every +delta remains in the running total from l through r, and the -delta after r removes it before the next index. Overlapping updates add naturally because their active intervals contribute simultaneously. The base array is separate: final[i] = A[i] + activeDelta[i] unless diff was initialized from A itself.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.final_value_without_base: The accumulated difference marks describe updates, not the original element unless the representation explicitly included A’s own differences.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.current_window_length: The running value is a sum of deltas, not a boundary distance. Many update intervals can be active at once.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sorted_update_count: No sorting or value comparison is involved. The state is determined only by positional start and stop events.

items.prompt: Order the operations for applying a batch of inclusive range-add updates with a difference array.
constraints: The base array A is retained separately.
Score is based on preserved adjacent relations.

elements.text: Initialize diff with zeros for all required boundaries.
For every update, add delta at l and subtract delta at r + 1 when that boundary exists.
Scan left to right, accumulating diff into the active delta.
Add the active delta to A[i] to produce the final value at i.
Emit the completed final array after the reconstruction scan.

feedback.reason: All endpoint events must be recorded before one cumulative reconstruction converts them into per-index effects.

blocks.text: The batch is deferred: update processing records only boundary events, and a later prefix scan turns those events into the delta active at each index.

items: Initialize the difference buffer to zero at every reconstructed boundary.
For each inclusive update [l, r] by delta, add delta at l and subtract delta at r + 1 when r + 1 lies in the buffer.
After every update is marked, scan left to right and add diff[i] to activeDelta.
At each i, produce final[i] = A[i] + activeDelta.
After the reconstruction scan completes, emit the completed final array.

blocks.title: Do not reconstruct between marks
blocks.text: Reconstructing or emitting before all events are recorded either repeats linear work or omits later updates. The O(1)-per-update benefit depends on one reconstruction after the complete batch.

items.prompt: For an inclusive update [l, n - 1], how should the stop mark be handled in a length-n diff array?
constraints: diff has indices 0 through n - 1 only.
The reconstruction scan ends at n - 1.

options.text: Write diff[n - 1] -= delta so the last element is not updated.
Write the stop mark at diff[0].
Write diff[l] += delta and omit the stop mark because r + 1 equals n, outside the reconstructed domain.
Sort diff and place the negative mark at its last value.

feedback.reason: An update that reaches the final index never needs to stop within the scanned domain.

blocks.text: The +delta must remain active through n - 1. A stop at r would cancel it before the last element, while wrapping to zero would corrupt the whole prefix. An alternative legal representation allocates n + 1 boundaries and writes the stop at diff[n], but a length-n array must guard the write.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.subtract_at_r: The stop boundary is after r, not at r. Subtracting at n - 1 removes the update from the final requested position.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.wrap_to_zero: Array boundaries do not wrap. A negative mark at zero would alter every reconstructed index.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_then_stop: Difference marks are positional events. Sorting destroys their boundary meaning.

items.prompt: Why are overlapping batch range additions not equivalent to maintaining one moving window?
constraints: All updates are known before reconstruction.
Many update ranges may overlap at one index.

options.text: Two mathematical intervals are never allowed to overlap in a window problem.
The difference array works only because update ranges are sorted by delta.
The difference array is equivalent to a window because neither stores any state.
The difference array superposes start and stop events for many ranges, while one window state represents only one currently maintained interval.

feedback.reason: Difference state represents the combined effects of many intervals through boundary events; a window tracks one evolving interval.

blocks.text: At an index, the active delta may include contributions from any number of overlapping updates. Those contributions are recovered by integrating all event marks. A moving window can overlap a previous window, but its algorithmic state still belongs to one current range and does not encode an arbitrary batch of deferred modifications.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.windows_cannot_overlap: Intervals may overlap in any problem. The distinction is state ownership, not a prohibition on geometric overlap.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.prefix_requires_sorting: The scan follows index order, but values and deltas need not be sorted. Event positions already define the order.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_auxiliary_state: A separate difference array stores O(n) boundary state. A window usually stores O(1) or bounded current-state data.

items.prompt: A developer sorts A before applying difference-array updates because they believe prefix accumulation requires sorted input. What happens?
constraints: Each update [l, r] names original positions.
The final result must preserve the original element order.

options.text: The positional ranges now refer to different elements, so the updates are applied to the wrong data.
Sorting changes every O(1) mark into O(n).
Sorting makes negative update deltas invalid.
Sorting automatically removes every r + 1 boundary.

feedback.reason: Difference arrays encode index boundaries in the original domain; sorting changes the ownership of those boundaries.

blocks.text: The algorithm needs a left-to-right index order for reconstruction, but it does not need values to be ordered. Reordering A changes which elements lie inside each update range even though the diff arithmetic still runs. Prefix accumulation and sortedness are separate concepts.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.diff_becomes_quadratic: The asymptotic cost of writing marks does not depend on value order. The failure is semantic, not a complexity change.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.negative_delta_forbidden: Positive and negative deltas are both valid. Sorting has no effect on their algebraic legality.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.stop_mark_disappears: Boundary positions still exist after sorting; they simply refer to the wrong elements for the original problem.

items.prompt: For u inclusive range-add updates on an array of length n, select the total time and extra space of a separate difference array followed by one reconstruction pass.
constraints: Each update writes at most two boundary marks.
The base array is retained separately.

feedback.reason: Each update performs constant endpoint work and one linear prefix scan materializes all final effects; the separate boundary buffer is linear.

blocks.text: Each of u updates writes at most two boundary entries, so all marks cost O(u). The reconstruction visits each of n positions once, adding O(n); the total is O(u + n). The separate difference buffer stores one value per reconstructed index (or n + 1 guarded boundaries), so it uses O(n) extra space under the prompt's accounting.

blocks.title: Why the other offered bounds are wrong
blocks.text: O(un) applies every update across an entire range and ignores endpoint encoding. O(u log n + n) adds a logarithmic update cost that two direct array writes do not have. O(n^2) is not a valid general bound in both independent parameters u and n. Space is not O(1) or O(log n) because the separate buffer is linear in n, and it is not O(un) because updates share the same boundary buffer instead of allocating a new array per update.

items.prompt: Which variation preserves the boundary-event idea but requires a genuinely two-dimensional encoding?
constraints: Many axis-aligned rectangle additions are applied to a matrix.
Only the final matrix is needed after all updates.

options.text: Use only one +delta at the rectangle’s top-left row and one -delta after its bottom row.
Use four signed corner marks per rectangle and integrate across both dimensions.
Sort all cells and apply the rectangle by value rank.
Maintain one moving rectangle and discard all prior updates.

feedback.reason: A rectangle has independent row and column boundaries, so its start/stop effect must be encoded at signed corners and integrated in two dimensions.

blocks.text: For an inclusive rectangle from (r1, c1) to (r2, c2), mark `diff[r1][c1] += delta`, `diff[r1][c2 + 1] -= delta`, `diff[r2 + 1][c1] -= delta`, and `diff[r2 + 1][c2 + 1] += delta`, omitting or guarding marks beyond the matrix boundary. Prefix-accumulating across both rows and columns then makes the two negative marks stop the effect after each axis, while the final positive corner corrects their double subtraction. The reconstructed delta is active exactly inside the rectangle. One-dimensional row endpoints cannot restrict columns, and sorting or one current rectangle loses spatial ownership of the batch.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_dimensional_endpoints_only: Row events alone apply the delta across entire rows and cannot restrict the affected columns. Both dimensions need boundaries.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_matrix_values: Rectangle membership is coordinate-based, not value-based. Sorting cells destroys the geometry.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.single_moving_rectangle: A single active rectangle cannot retain the superposed effects of many deferred updates.

items.prompt: For an inclusive range addition [l,r] by delta in a difference array, which boundary update stops the effect after r?

options.text: Add -delta at difference[r+1], when that boundary exists.
Add -delta at difference[r], which stops before r.
Add -delta at difference[l-1], reversing the update's start.
No end marker is needed because the final prefix handles it automatically.

feedback.reason: The reconstructed running sum changes at l and changes back at the exclusive boundary immediately after r.

blocks.text: The update is half-open in its difference representation: +delta begins at l, while -delta at r+1 prevents positions after r from inheriting the range addition.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.r: Placing the marker at r would exclude index r from the intended inclusive update.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.l_minus_one: That changes the prefix before the range rather than ending the range.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_end: Without an end marker, the update leaks into every later position.

items.prompt: After applying many range updates to a difference array, what operation materializes the final value at each index?

options.text: Take one prefix sum over the difference array.
Sort the update records and read their endpoints directly.
Take a maximum over each adjacent pair of markers.
Take suffix sums from the final index toward zero.

feedback.reason: Each difference entry describes a change in the active update total, so a running prefix restores the active total itself.

blocks.text: The range-update phase is O(number of updates), and the reconstruction phase is O(n). The difference array is an encoding of changes, not the final values.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_updates: Sorting does not accumulate overlapping deltas at each position.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.pairwise_max: Updates combine by addition, not by a local maximum.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reverse_prefix: The marker convention is defined for a forward prefix reconstruction.

items.prompt: For an inclusive update adding delta to [l,r], what first difference-array marker begins its effect?

options.text: Add +delta at difference[l].
Add +delta at difference[r], excluding earlier requested positions.
Add -delta at difference[l].
The running prefix will infer the start without a marker.

feedback.reason: The running reconstructed value changes exactly at the range's left boundary.

blocks.text: The matching -delta marker at r+1 stops the effect after the inclusive right endpoint. Both markers are derived from the half-open reconstruction convention.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.plus_at_r: That would delay the update until r.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.minus_at_l: A negative marker would remove rather than add the range value.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_marker: Without a start marker the running sum cannot begin the update at l.

items.prompt: How do overlapping range additions combine in a difference array?

options.text: Their start and end deltas add at shared boundaries, and one prefix reconstruction accumulates the total.
The latest update replaces all earlier updates.
Only the largest delta survives at each index.
Each update requires a separate final array even when addition is the operation.

feedback.reason: Difference encoding is linear under addition: independent changes sum before reconstruction.

blocks.text: This is why many batch updates can be recorded in O(1) marker work per update and materialized in one O(n) pass.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.max_only: The operation is addition, not maximum.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.separate_arrays: One combined difference array is sufficient for additive updates.

items.prompt: What boundary issue must be handled when writing the -delta marker at r+1?

options.text: Provide a boundary slot or guard the write when r is the final index.
Always write at index -1 when r is final.
Skip the +delta start marker instead.
Wrap r+1 to index zero so the update remains circular.

feedback.reason: The exclusive end boundary may be exactly n, outside the n-element value array.

blocks.text: A length n+1 difference buffer naturally supports a marker at n. If the implementation uses length n, skip the end marker only when it lies outside the represented reconstruction.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.write_before_zero: Negative indexing is not the after-range boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.omit_start: The update still needs to begin at l.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.wrap_around: Wrap-around changes a linear range into a circular one.

items.prompt: During reconstruction, what does the running total after processing index i represent?

options.text: The sum of all range-update deltas active at position i.
Only updates that will begin after i.
The number of marker entries, ignoring their signed values.
The original array value before any update.

feedback.reason: A prefix of changes accumulates the current active update total.

blocks.text: Assign that running total to the final value or add it to a base array according to the problem. Signed deltas, not marker count, determine the result.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.future_delta: Future markers have not entered the running prefix yet.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.marker_count: Positive and negative changes can cancel.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.original_value: Difference reconstruction represents updates, not necessarily the original base value.
